product_offering.core_offering: Clay is an AI-native go-to-market (GTM) development platform that combines 150+ data providers, AI research agents (Claygents), intent signals, and workflow orchestration into a single product. It enables sales, marketing, and RevOps teams to automate prospect research, lead enrichment, signal-based prioritization, and outbound campaigns through a unified table-based environment with API and AI assistant access.
product_offering.differentiator: Aggregates 150+ data providers in a single waterfall; native AI research agent (Claygent) that automates prospecting and enrichment; code-level extensibility via Clay Functions and Clay MCP; one platform combining data enrichment, AI research, signals, and outreach (Sequencer); large and engaged GTM engineering community (40K+) producing templates and playbooks.
product_offering.functional_benefit: Higher data match rates via multi-provider waterfall; reduced manual research time through Claygent automation; programmable workflows that replace stitched-together point tools; faster outbound iteration with AI formatting and Sculptor co-pilot; consolidated cost vs. paying for many individual data and outreach tools.
product_offering.problem_solved: Fragmented GTM data and tooling, slow and manual prospect research, low data match rates and high cost per enriched record, lack of programmatic control for RevOps/GTM engineers, and the difficulty of consolidating enrichment, signals, AI research, and outbound into one workflow.
quantifiable_outcome: ~$100M ARR at time of Series C
150+ data providers integrated into waterfall enrichment
product_offering.product_overview: Clay is a single unified GTM development platform that brings together data enrichment, AI agents, intent signals, and orchestration in one product rather than a platform-plus-modules architecture sold separately. Its core surface is the Clay table, which combines Waterfall enrichment across 150+ data providers, Claygents for AI-led research, Signals and Intent for tracking buyer behavior, AI Formatting for cleaning records, and Clay Functions for reusable logic. On top of this core, Clay layers execution-oriented modules — Ads (LinkedIn/Meta/Google audience sync), Audiences (CRM + product + intent unification), Sequencer (native email outreach), Sculptor (natural-language co-pilot), Clay MCP (exposing workflows to external AI assistants), and Clay for Salesforce (Salesforce-native workflows). The company also operates sub-brands such as Clay University (education and certifications), Sculpt (its annual GTM conference), and acquired Avenue to embed intent-signal alerting. Together these products let GTM engineers build, test, and scale automated revenue workflows end-to-end.

profiles.name: Kareem Amin
profiles.overview: Co-founder and CEO of Clay who positioned the company as a 'system of action' balancing human creativity with AI automation and helped coin the 'GTM engineering' category.
profiles.profile_commentary: Kareem Amin is co-founder and CEO of Clay, leading the company's positioning around treating sales as a creative act and AI-augmented workflow automation. Under his leadership, Clay grew from $1M ARR to $100M ARR in two years, raised a $100M Series C at a $3.1B valuation in August 2025, and reached roughly a $5B valuation by January 2026. He is also a featured guest on investor and industry podcasts (e.g., Sequoia podcast) representing Clay's public voice.

profiles.name: Varun Anand
profiles.overview: Co-Founder of Clay who defined the 'negative maintenance' business philosophy and serves as a frequent author on Clay's blog covering GTM engineering and Clay's internal use of Clay.
profiles.profile_commentary: Varun Anand is co-founder of Clay and also serves as Head of Operations, contributing to product and operational philosophy including the 'negative maintenance' approach to GTM engineering. He is a frequent author on Clay's blog, writing on GTM alpha, GTM engineering, and how Clay uses Clay internally. He publicly endorsed the 2X acquisition of The Kiln, one of Clay's top-performing go-to-market engineering partners.

recent_move.description: Closed a $100M Series C led by CapitalG at a $3.1B valuation in August 2025, bringing total funding to approximately $204M and providing capital to scale the GTM engineering category.

Launched six major platform products at Sculpt 2025 in September 2025: Sculptor AI co-pilot, Claygent Builder, Claygent Connectors, Audiences, Sequencer, and Web Intent, extending Clay from enrichment to full GTM orchestration.

Clay announced it will significantly expand its Manhattan headquarters by leasing 163,095 square feet of office space at 11 Madison Avenue in the Flatiron District, with plans to create 498 new full-time jobs over five years and invest $50 million in research and development activity in New York State, supported by up to $9.96 million in Excelsior Jobs Program tax credits from Empire State Development.
recent_move.title: NYC Headquarters Expansion

expansion_highlight.description: NYC expansion plan tied to 498 new jobs over five years alongside a $50M R&D investment commitment, announced April 2026, signals aggressive organizational scaling.

Sculpt 2025 introduced six new products (Sculptor, Claygent Builder, Claygent Connectors, Audiences, Sequencer, Web Intent) and early-2026 added Clay Functions and Clay MCP, expanding the platform from data enrichment into full GTM workflow orchestration and AI agent distribution.

EMEA-specific data partnerships with Lusha (verified phone, EMEA-compliant data, March 2026), Beauhurst (UK/Germany funding data, March 2026), and Ocean.io, plus GDPR/CCPA compliance, indicate a deliberate push into European markets.
Clay Partner Program launched August 2025 with solution, integration, creator, and startup tiers, formalizing the indirect sales channel alongside Clay Studio Partners demandDrive and Cobalt Keys.

January 2025 acquisition of Avenue (intent signal workflow automation) and acquisition of The Kiln (now part of 2X, a Clay Studio Partner) suggest continued tuck-in M&A to deepen agent and agency capacity.

March 2026 pricing restructure separating Data Credits (company/people data) and Actions (enrichments, AI tasks, workflow operations) with advanced features moved behind a $495/month tier is designed to capture more value from heavy-usage enterprise accounts.
Raised approximately $204M across disclosed rounds through August 2025, with two tender offers (Sept 2025 at $1.5B, Jan 2026 at $5B), sustaining primary capital availability for continued expansion.
